policy_verdict.explanation: The complete open parent group passed the merchant breadth and membership checks; suppress duplicate invoice-level contact and open one relationship escalation.

proposal.diagnosis: All nine invoices carrying parent_group_id GRP-SURYODAYA — spread across six separate payer entities in different cities but sharing one group parent — are simultaneously unpaid with zero contacts made, and their replies describe the same account-level condition rather than nine independent delinquencies: payables consolidated to a single central desk, approval limits rewritten, vendor masters being rebuilt at the centre, files already passed sent back for a fresh look, and local staff who prepare the voucher but can no longer see or release it. Two members (ASH-2026-0005, ASH-2026-0008) are simply silent, which is consistent with the same central freeze reaching entities whose local contacts have nothing to add. The inferred cause is one group-level payables centralisation/re-approval event, not nine separate credit failures.
proposal.reasoning: The signal is only visible across records. Each entity's prior settlement history shows consistent, if late, full payment behaviour — these are not chronically bad payers individually. What changed is common: multiple distinct legal entities, distinct cities, distinct named contacts and roles, all reporting in their own words that release authority has moved away from them to a single group office, that queued items were reopened for re-review, and that no one local can name a holder or a date. Independent delinquencies would not produce that convergence of language across six payer_ids in one snapshot. Several of the replies explicitly redirect us to a head office and one asks us not to follow up weekly because the answer will be identical — which is exactly the condition under which per-invoice chasing generates noise at each unit while reaching no decision-maker. Countervailing points that hold confidence below certainty: no dispute is recorded on any of these records, the entities' overdue positions vary widely in maturity, and two members carry no prose at all, so their inclusion rests on group membership and shared silence rather than direct statement. The cause remains an inference from correlated prose; it is not confirmed. On that basis individual per-invoice contact appears counterproductive and one consolidated relationship escalation addressed at the group level is the proportionate step, subject to the deterministic policy check validating the full group.
